_note: Fictional papers and hand-written statements. These cases pin the behaviour of backend/llm/claimGuard.js and validateIntelligence so a later change cannot silently reopen a closed gap. They say nothing about accuracy on real summaries; that needs the human benchmark (docs/evaluation/HUMAN_BENCHMARK.md). Cases marked known are limitations that the current rules do not handle, kept here so they stay visible.

P1.text: On the benchmark test split Sparse Attention Routing (SAR) reaches 87.4 percent exact-match accuracy, compared with 79.1 percent for the dense baseline. Removing the moving-average update reduces accuracy to 83.0 percent. SAR did not improve results on short questions.
SAR replaces the dense attention of every fourth transformer layer. We train on 38 billion tokens for 3 epochs using 5-fold cross-validation on the development set.
We evaluated only English text and a single model scale of 7 billion parameters. The gains may concentrate on questions whose evidence lies more than 64k tokens from the question.

P2.text: In a pilot study of 24 patients, the denoiser lowered the median heart-rate error from 6.2 to 3.9 beats per minute (range 1.1-9.8). The difference suggests a benefit but the study was not powered for significance.
Latency was 12 ms per window on the reference laptop. Battery drain was not measured. The device was not compared with a commercial monitor.

P3.text: The change was −3.2 points on the test set.
